title: Jannik Sinner vs Jakub Menšík, Jiří Lehečka vs Arthur Fils Preview: Head-to-Head, Prediction for Qatar Open 2026 - NewsBreak
text:
By Sagnik Datta ,
1 hours ago
The 2026 Qatar Open will see the four quarterfinals play out on February 19. In the bottom half of the draw, the second seed, Jannik Sinner, will face the rising Czech sensation, Jakub Menšík, whereas the eighth-seeded Jiří Lehečka will take on a returning Arthur Fils in the last eight.
Let’s take a look at the two quarterfinal matchups in the bottom half of the draw.
Jannik Sinner vs Jakub Menšík Second-seeded Jannik Sinner is all set to face off against Jakub Menšík in the quarterfinal of the 2026 Qatar Open. Sinner has been in pristine form in Doha so far, winning 6-1, 6-4 against Tomáš Macháč in the first round, followed by an equally impressive 6-3, 7-5 win over Alexei Popyrin in the second round.
Meanwhile, Menšík began his campaign with a 6-7 (8), 6-2, 6-4 win against the British qualifier, Jan Choinski, in the first round, followed by a dominant 6-3, 6-2 win against Zhang Zhizhen.
The head-to-head record is 0-0, as neither player has played the other on the Tour. Sinner has won 82% of his first serve points in his two matches in Doha, with Menšík winning 77% of the first-serve points. While the Czech player has been broken twice at this event, Sinner has yet to face even a break point after two matches.
Sinner will have the advantage with his second serve, as the Italian has won 79% of his points behind that shot, whereas Menšík has won 57% of the second-serve points. Yet, facing a breakpoint and current form, the second seed is the firm favorite in the upcoming match.
Pick – Sinner to win in straight sets
Jiří Lehečka vs Arthur Fils Another quarterfinal on the day will see the eighth-seeded Jiří Lehečka take on the young Frenchman, Arthur Fils, in the quarterfinals at the 2026 Qatar Open. Lehečka started his event with a 6-3, 6-3 win over Jenson Brooksby, after which he registered another dominant 6-2, 6-1 win over Zizou Bergs.
On the other hand, Fils started with a hard-fought 6-7 (5), 6-3, 6-4 win over Kamil Majchrzak, followed by a 6-1, 7-6 (6) against compatriot Quentin Halys in the second round.
The head-to-head is 1-1, with Lehečka winning their recent encounter at the 2025 Canadian Open, 3-6, 6-3, 6-4. Both of them have served well, with Lehečka winning 80 percent of the first serve points and Fils winning 75% of the first serve points. One area where the Czech is significantly ahead of his French opponent is break-point conversion, with the Czech at 73% and Fils at 46%.
Lehečka has a superior record in Doha, reaching the semifinals twice in the last two years, including a win over Carlos Alcaraz last year, making him the favorite to win the upcoming match.
Pick – Lehečka to win in straight sets
